summary.headline: NBCC standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore (8.77% margin) on 10% revenue growth to INR 1,823 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR 1,823 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore and PAT rose 32% to INR 151 crore, helped by marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,260 crore, with a consolidated order book of INR 1,27,000 crore and INR 1,600 crore of orders secured in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore of new awards over the next 2-3 quarters, but several large awards (GPRA 5 colonies, J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) have slipped repeatedly. Management also announced the HSCC merger into NBCC and an SPV for a proposed CPSE REIT.

segments.name: PMC / redevelopment (standalone order book)
segments.commentary: Standalone order book split is about 60% redevelopment and 40% PMC. Management says redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of total revenue, and PMC fees are 8% plus 1% marketing on Amrapali.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Management expects about INR 500 crore of real estate revenue this year from land, completed inventory and WIP sales. Bharat Business Park was fully sold, raising about INR 10,000 crore across three auctions.

segments.name: HSCC (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue dipped because HSCC foreclosed a Maharashtra health project quoted at about 2% margin, which management says cost about INR 300 crore of top line. Management is merging HSCC into NBCC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore reiterated; management referred to INR 16,000-17,000 crore in parts of the call.
Standalone FY27 revenue guided at INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 revenue around INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore (consolidated basis per management).
PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore for FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY28 and about INR 2,000 crore for FY29, on a consolidated basis.
Margin guidance: EBITDA at least 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

Awards guided at INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year (including Supertech about INR 10,000 crore, J&K about INR 3,500 crore, Rajasthan Mandapam about INR 3,500 crore), against an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore target.
GPRA 5 colonies (Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj, DIZ, Lakshmi Bai Nagar) order of about INR 30,000 crore expected; management says cabinet approval is pending.
Redevelopment fund generation of INR 30,000-35,000 crore expected this year, sale-linked and construction-linked, with cash collected over about two years.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 Amrapali is awarded and in execution, with one tower at the 20th floor using Mivan shuttering and others at the 13th floor; Phase 1 has 23 of 24 projects completed.
Standalone order book: about INR 10,000 crore of balance work across GPRA 7 packages, to be completed within about 18-24 months.
Gurugram Sector 37-D: contractor mobilised and test piles done; revised plan and EC approval pending, with sales expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Ghitorni: final lease agreement in process; consultant tender expected to be finalised this quarter; revenue after handover in about two years.
Business Park Tower purchase is construction-linked; only 10% first instalment paid so far, with the balance tied to construction milestones over about two years.
Dubai: 66 housing units under construction on a purchased land parcel; developer licence in hand; construction tender expected in October.
Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, site mobilised and work started; two more packages pending tender.
demand_pricing: Africa Avenue auction for 262 residential units drew about 2,900 participants; auction postponed on a technical issue and expected in August. Vinayak Mandir auction targeted for September and Palanji area for September-October. Management expects INR 5,000-6,000 crore from Africa Avenue sales.
Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

Recent wins: Odisha schools INR 253 crore, J&K campus INR 171 crore, New AP Bhavan INR 106 crore (Q1); Seychelles housing about INR 620 crore, RBI Amravati about INR 780 crore, Rajasthan science labs about INR 431 crore (July-August).
International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited INR 6,500 crore last quarter; management did not reconcile the comparison

qa_highlights.question: Why are the large orders (about INR 50,000 crore GPRA 5 colonies plus other large orders) delayed, and when will they come? Is FY27 and FY28 revenue still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: GPRA 5 colonies (about INR 30,000 crore) has cleared the group of ministers and PIB and is with Cabinet; management says it is a matter of time. At least one or two contracts expected in Q2 and major ones in Q3. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and said it is adhering to it.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move over the next two to three quarters, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise because redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of revenue. Guided EBITDA minimum 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA rise sharply while work and consultancy expenses fell from INR 3,412 crore in Q4 FY26 to INR 1,536 crore in Q1 FY27 (standalone)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the jump to marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale, which carry low associated expenses. Further marketing fees are expected from Africa Avenue, Vinayak Mandir, Sarojini Nagar (7 GPRA) and 1% on Amrapali inventory sales of about INR 4,000-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone and PMC revenue growth look slow, and what are the FY27-FY29 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited HSCC dropping a low-margin (about 2%) Maharashtra health project, costing about INR 300 crore of top line, and said Q1 is seasonally slow. Standalone FY27 revenue INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 about INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore. PAT guidance INR 1,100-1,200 crore FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore FY28, about INR 2,000 crore FY29 (consolidated).

qa_highlights.question: Is the Business Park tower purchase a cash drain, and what are the cash timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the first 10% instalment is paid; the rest is construction-linked over about two years. Management said cash will go out as CapEx and cited an auction price rise from a base of INR 39,100 to about INR 66,000 on the ground floor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CPSE REIT plan, timeline and investment needed?
qa_highlights.answer: NBCC approved an SPV in principle, subject to ministry and DIPAM approval, to hold three rentable assets totalling about 75,000 sq ft. No timeline was given; management said a national REIT will be launched only after a considerable portfolio (across CPSEs, est. INR 40,000-50,000 crore across five or six REITs) is assembled.

qa_highlights.question: Why have big awards (J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) slipped, and is funding the constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited government clearances, DPR approvals, seed money and about 18-20 statutory approvals. Seed money is being arranged by NBCC on some projects and by clients on others; a HUDCO MoU is in place. Management revised awards guidance to INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year from an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore.

risks_watch: Repeated slippage of large awards: GPRA 5 colonies (about INR 30,000 crore, Cabinet pending), J&K (about INR 3,500-4,000 crore tender), MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore, now Q3) and Supertech (about INR 10,000 crore). Management cut 2026 award guidance to INR 20,000-25,000 crore from INR 30,000-32,000 crore.
FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore against standalone Q1 revenue of INR 1,823 crore; analysts questioned the run rate and Q3 Delhi GRAP construction curbs.
Earnings quality: Q1 EBITDA gain driven partly by one-off marketing fees from Bharat Business Park; FY27 PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore needs roughly 2x the Q1 run rate of INR 151 crore.

Cash and seed money: cash of INR 666 crore at 30 June; the comparison to INR 6,500 crore last quarter was not reconciled. Seed money needs for new projects and the construction-linked Business Park payments are open questions.

Real estate and REIT execution: Gurugram 37-D sales depend on revised plan and EC approval; Ghitorni lease is still being finalised; the REIT has no timeline. Revenue from Ghitorni and 37-D comes only after about two years.
key_quotes: Definitely, our margin is going to increase.
So, due to various approvals, the project got delayed. Two reason. One is fund. Other one is various approvals.
Definitely, it is going to happen. We have the figures; I am not making commitments casually.
I am still committing to these figures, and whatever I am saying, those figures will be achieved.
summary.management_tone: Confident and emphatic on the FY27 revenue and PAT targets, repeatedly saying they are backed by internal calculations and that the company has backup plans. Noticeably cautious and evasive on the timing of the large pending awards (GPRA 5, MAHAPREIT, Supertech, J&K), attributing delays to government approvals, Cabinet processes and state government working speed, and giving no firm dates beyond quarter-level estimates.

growth.why: Management reiterated consolidated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore (midpoint about 16%) and guided FY28 to about INR 21,000 crore, backed by a INR 1,27,000 crore consolidated order book and identified tenders, but several large awards have slipped repeatedly and the order-award target was cut to INR 20,000-25,000 crore from INR 30,000-32,000 crore.
